Built for ML Teams working with messy real-world data 
 Pause training, mine live loss signals to surface mislabels, class imbalance & outliers, then curate your image, video, text & LiDAR data, without restarting.

 Overview

WeightsLab hooks into your existing PyTorch training loop and exposes a live UI where you can inspect per-sample signals, edit the dataset, and steer training. Without restarting.

 WeightsLab in Motion
 
 
 
 

 Quickstart
For a detailed installation guide and advanced configuration: Documentation.

 1. Install & Launch 
 

With uv, choose the PyTorch build with --torch-backend ( auto , cpu , cu126 , ...), not --extra-index-url : see the uv install notes.

 

 [!TIP]
 Studio with HTTP Secure Deployment. Run before starting this command to set certificates.
 

 2. Start 

 In the cloud directly 

 

 Or Wrap your training script locally 
 

 [!TIP]
 Quick examples to get started
 
 Explore our sandbox.

 How can you use it ?

 1. Find bad data fast Pause training mid-run before bad data are learnt, sort samples by loss, spot mislabels and outliers before they impact your model.

 2. Fix and resume without re-starting Relabel or drop samples live, then continue training from the same checkpoint.

 3. Catch model regressions early on Analyze per-sample loss trajectories to see exactly where the model is struggling.

 Agent: chat with your training run (OpenCode) 

WeightsLab ships two distinct agent surfaces: the backend SDK agent for data-manipulation
queries, and a local OpenCode-backed agent with a full bash/file
toolset that can restart training, edit your code, and run recurring /loop monitoring
jobs. See the Agent docs for
how the two connect, how to point either one at a local model, and the full /loop 
reference.

 

 Contributing and OnBoarding

New here (human or AI coding agent)? Start with AGENTS.md; it
captures the cross-repo architecture (weightslab backend ↔ weights studio
frontend via the shared proto), the module maps, the integration pattern, where tests live, and the gotchas that aren't obvious from
any single file. It's the fastest way to orient before a first change and contribution.

 Community

We're building a community of ML engineers around data-centric training tooling.
Interested in contributing or just want to say hi? → hello [at] graybx [dot] com

install.title: Quickstart
install.html:
For a detailed installation guide and advanced configuration: Documentation.

1. Install & Launch

pip install weightslab
# or, with uv
uv add weightslab         # in a uv project (uv run weightslab start)
uv pip install weightslab --torch-backend=auto  # in any virtual environment
uvx --torch-backend=auto weightslab start       # just the CLI / Studio UI

With uv, choose the PyTorch build with --torch-backend (auto, cpu, cu126, ...), not --extra-index-url: see the uv install notes.

weightslab start ./my_experiment_directory # optional: open the UI on an experiment directory

[!TIP] Studio with HTTP Secure Deployment. Run before starting this command to set certificates.

weightslab se  # set certificates for encryption

2. Start

In the cloud directly

Or Wrap your training script locally

# wrap the objects in your training script

import weightslab as wl
...
model  = wl.watch_or_edit(model, flag='model')
optim  = wl.watch_or_edit(optim, flag='opt')
loss   = wl.watch_or_edit(loss, flag='signal', name="loss", per_sample=True, log=True)
loader = wl.watch_or_edit(dataset, flag='data', loader_name="train")
...
wl.serve(serving_grpc=True, serving_cli=False)  # also serves Weights Studio and opens it in your browser
...

[!TIP] Quick examples to get started

weightslab start example            # classification (default)
weightslab start example --cls      # classification
weightslab start example --seg      # segmentation
weightslab start example --det      # detection
weightslab start example --clus     # clustering

Explore our sandbox.
